step1_analysis.description: A symmetrical current-mirror OTA with a differential input pair and two identical output branches. It serves as the core amplifier for an adaptive ENG recording system, providing high output impedance and transconductance to drive subsequent filtering or adaptation stages.

paper_reference.title: An Adaptive ENG Amplifier for Tripolar Cuff Electrodes

voltage_gain.description: Open-loop AC voltage gain in the ENG signal band (e.g., at 1 kHz).

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current = 20uA -> Id1 = 10uA. Gm = sqrt(2 * 270u * 10 * 10u) = 232 uS. Rout = ro_p || ro_n = 1/(0.1*10u) || 1/(0.1*10u) = 500 kOhm. Av = Gm * Rout = 116 V/V = 41.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using SKY130 parameters. The paper's 54 dB might have used longer channel lengths (higher Rout) or lower bias currents.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency at which the open-loop voltage gain drops to 0 dB.

sky130_expected.calculation: fu = Gm / (2 * pi * Cload). With Cload = 10pF, fu = 232uS / (2 * pi * 10pF) = 3.69 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bandwidth is heavily dependent on the load capacitance. 3.7 MHz is more than sufficient to cover the 10 kHz ENG band.

power_dissipation.description: Total DC power consumption of the amplifier.

paper_reported.value: Low power emphasized for inside the cuff

sky130_expected.calculation: Total VDD current = 5 branches * 10uA = 50uA. Tail current (VSS) = 20uA. Power = (50uA * 1.8V) + (20uA * 1.8V) = 126 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on a 20uA tail current and 1:1 current mirror ratios across the 5 branches.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the amplifier to ensure stability in closed-loop configurations.

sky130_expected.calculation: Single dominant pole at output node. Phase shifts from 180 (inverting) to 90 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As a single-stage OTA, it naturally has a ~90 degree phase margin when loaded with a capacitor.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure open-loop AC gain, bandwidth, phase margin, transient swing, and DC power. A dual supply is used to accommodate the hardcoded GND at the non-inverting input, and large inductors are used to set the output DC bias to VDD/2 without loading the AC signal.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Adaptive ENG Amplifier OTA Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u

* DUT
XM3 N1 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM7 IO2 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N0 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM6 IO1 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM4 N0 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N5 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM2 N5 GND IFI GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM9 IO1 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM1 N1 VI IFI GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM10 IO2 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}

* Power Supplies (Dual supply to handle GND at XM2 gate)
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 -1.8
I_tail IFI VSS 20u

* Input Signal (1mV peak sine at 1kHz + AC 1 for Bode plot)
V_VI VI 0 DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 1m 1k)

* Output DC Bias and AC Load
* Biasing outputs at 0.9V to keep output transistors in saturation
V_out_bias OUT_BIAS 0 0.9
L_bias1 OUT_BIAS IO1 1G
C_load1 IO1 0 10p
L_bias2 OUT_BIAS IO2 1G
C_load2 IO2 0 10p

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = (-i(VVDD) * 1.8) + (-i(VVSS) * 1.8)
print power

* 2. AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1 100MEG
let gain_db = vdb(IO1)
let phase = 180/PI * cph(v(IO1))

meas ac gain_1k find gain_db at=1k
meas ac gain_10k find gain_db at=10k
meas ac ugf when gain_db=0 fall=1
meas ac phase_at_ugf find phase when gain_db=0 fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis
tran 10u 5m
meas tran v_out_max max v(IO1)
meas tran v_out_min min v(IO1)
let v_out_ptp = v_out_max - v_out_min
print v_out_ptp

quit
.endc
